Figure 2:Overview of MEMO.
The motion model translates and rotates each Gaussian and its oriented normal (arrows) from the canonical state to timett.
Training backpropagates (red)ℒRGB\mathcal{L}_{\text{RGB}},ℒD\mathcal{L}_{D}between the geometric and depth normals𝐍g\mathbf{N}_{g}and𝐍d\mathbf{N}_{d}, andℒN\mathcal{L}_{N}between𝐍d\mathbf{N}_{d}and the oriented normals𝐍o\mathbf{N}_{o}.
Mesh extraction follows Gaussian Wrapping[21]: tetrahedralizing the pivots, evaluating the vacancy field at each pivot (red occupied, blue vacant), and recovering its 0.5 level set with marching tetrahedra.

Figure 4:200 sampled tracks of Lego from our initialization with a single first-frame anchor, over the first-frame mesh.
The fitted trajectories follow the bucket through its full sweep before training begins.
Dots are track positions every tenth frame, and curves of the same color are the fitted trajectories.

Figure 5:Meshes of MEMO and the baselines, rendered from novel viewpoints.
The top rows show three Blender-Moments scenes beside the ground truth, and the bottom rows show the real scenes Flame salmon and Yoga, with each method’s color render inset and the crop outlined in red.
Deformable-3DGS represents the appearance-only methods, as its meshes look the best among them, and the gray dots are Gaussian floaters.
MEMO produces clean surfaces and preserves fine details such as facial features and Lego studs, where D-2DGS leaves noise and holes and DG-Mesh oversmooths.
D-2DGS fails on Yoga, as its render shows.

Figure 6:Novel views of fast motion on Blender-Moments, Neural 3D Video, and SelfCap.
On real scenes, panels crop the moving part, with the full frame inset and the crop outlined in red.
MEMO keeps the limbs, hands, and face sharp, where the baselines blur or break them.

(a)Motion recovery of thin, fast-moving parts.
Left: static thin structures, such as the bucket cables of Lego and the brake cables of Bicycle, are cleanly reconstructed.
Right: fast-moving thin structures are smeared or lost, since the initialization may miss their tracks (Sec.A).
On Lego, the rotating knob (right) is lost, while the static knob beside it is recovered, and on Bicycle the spinning wheel spokes are lost.

(a)Motion recovery of thin, fast-moving parts.
Left: static thin structures, such as the bucket cables of Lego and the brake cables of Bicycle, are cleanly reconstructed.
Right: fast-moving thin structures are smeared or lost, since the initialization may miss their tracks (Sec.A).
On Lego, the rotating knob (right) is lost, while the static knob beside it is recovered, and on Bicycle the spinning wheel spokes are lost.

(b)Albedo and shading ambiguity.
Left: the edge of the sunlit patch on the vase in Yoga leaves a ridge in the mesh.
Right: the painted decals on Toyota leave a relief in the mesh.
In both, a sharp appearance boundary, from lighting in Yoga and from texture in Toyota, is partly explained as geometry.

(c)Narrow camera baselines.
Cut roasted beef and Sear steak share the kitchen and the front-facing rig of Neural 3D Video.
Left: in Cut roasted beef, the window blind is reconstructed flat.
Right: in Sear steak, some of its slats bulge toward the cameras, which see them with little parallax.

Figure S3:Ground truth and test renders of Spiderman and Flame salmon with the default number of interior inducing timesMM, withM/2M/2andM/4M/4, and without the trajectory fit.
Insets show the full Flame salmon frames, with the crop outlined in red.
Spiderman’s hands and Flame salmon’s torch smear atM/2M/2and break up atM/4M/4, while the defaultMMkeeps them sharp.
Without the trajectory fit, both scenes lose their moving parts, although the PSNR of the real scene barely changes.

Figure S4:Meshes of three real ablation scenes with no regularizers, only withℒD\mathcal{L}_{D}, only withℒN\mathcal{L}_{N}, with both (the default), and with the multi-view densification scheme of static Gaussian Wrapping.
All meshes were rendered from the test camera.
WithoutℒD\mathcal{L}_{D}, broad surfaces such as the blinds break into ridges and detached slats. WithoutℒN\mathcal{L}_{N}, surfaces are noisy and fragmented.
The multi-view scheme opens holes or distorts the geometry in textureless regions.

Figure S5:Blender-Moments meshes of MEMO extracted by our marching tetrahedra and by the extraction routes of the baselines, TSDF fusion of the rendered depth and Poisson reconstruction from the Gaussian centers and normals, beside the ground truth.
Marching tetrahedra preserves thin and detailed structures, TSDF fusion roughens and breaks them, and Poisson reconstruction melts them into smooth blobs or, on Spiderman, shatters the mesh.
Figure S6:The nine Blender-Moments scenes, each shown as a training image beside its ground-truth mesh at one frame.
